requirements_summary: Workloads: hard-real-time trading assistant (chat), streaming risk scoring, nightly reranking and embeddings for fast search.
Latency SLOs: trading-critical p95 <= 80ms, p99 <= 200ms for 256 tokens; analytics lane p95 <= 350ms.
Throughput guarantees: sustain 6k tokens/sec typical; burst up to 30k tokens/sec for short bursts (<=30s) without priority impact.
Reserved GPU planning: start with 12 A100-equiv reserved, ramp to 24 then 48 tied to pass/fail of SLA acceptance tests.
SLA negotiation points: explicit p99 measurement windows, credits for breach, maintenance blackout times, rollback guarantees on model rollouts.
Traffic shaping & priority lanes: per-route token/QPS quotas, weighted-latency-aware queueing, emergency throttles, lane reweight APIs.
Tenant isolation: per-tenant KV cache partitions, dedicated lane reservations, memory and compute capping at pod/instance level.
Noisy-neighbor controls: soft preemption of background lanes, hard caps on GPU utilization per tenant, and cache eviction policies per-tenant.
Per-route quotas & metering: token-level metering with exports for billing and chargeback; alerting on >80% route usage.
Fallback strategies: quantified fallback to quantized model variants, route to cold standby cluster, or queue admission control during overload.
Observability: fine-grained histograms (per-lane, per-route), request traces, cache hit/miss rates, and per-GPU utilization dashboards.
Security/compliance: BYOK KMS, SAML SSO, audit logs to SIEM, data residency assurances for EU desks behind private deployment option.
Operational runbook: market-open playbook to throttle non-critical lanes, steps to escalate noisy-neighbor events, and rollback procedures.
Acceptance testing: Redwood to provide a PoC plan (48h soak + synthetic market-open spike) and pass criteria for going GA.
